title: Modeli
type: Scribe and divine spellcaster · Veilguard founder
dek: An inexperienced scribe who runs toward a harbor attack, then tries to become worthy of divine trust without accepting that command must reduce people to numbers.

facts.Affiliation: Founding participant in the New Vanguard / Veilguard
facts.Outlook: Listen, preserve people and learn without pretending certainty
facts.Limits: Test answers are hypothetical; later plans remain unfinished

body:
Modeli’s first venture beyond Pristinia begins with stew, a drink and the hope that the more confident adventurers can handle any trouble. When smoke and screaming come, he runs toward them. His later place in the Veilguard grows from the tension between wanting to protect people and fearing what the work will make him.

The scribe runs toward the fire

At the harbor attack, Modeli looks first for ways to stop the fire spreading and get civilians to safety. He tells the company he has mostly been a scribe and has tried the training dungeon only once. He offers support to the front fighters rather than claiming to be one.

His anger at the attackers is harsher than his inexperience suggests. He demands that they leave, then wants the threat removed. Afterward the fight feels good to him: he thinks about how powerless he had been when the Rahu came and calls this victory justice. Days later he is troubled by his own pride and satisfaction. The question is his, even while he believes the people he defended needed help.

A student already carrying grief

At another encounter he moves between Aionia and a person holding a purple crystal, saying he came through the Rahu lines to serve the pantheon and protect Pristinia. Afterward he promises to remember what he has heard and blames himself for Serath’s death. The blame is his testimony, not a settled account of every cause of the loss.

He reaches the selection tests visibly exhausted from watching over a body. Kumai’s mockery does not make him docile. He asks the veteran to teach rather than merely belittle the people who have come to learn. He wants to become worthy of his blessings and needs instruction before there is another corpse to watch over.

Listening and refusing the offered choices

Modeli defines leadership as listening closely enough to choose well, including knowing when to ask someone else for help. Wisdom means being willing to adapt. When Kumai offers imagined sacrifices, he rejects the assumption that those choices exhaust what a leader can do.

He refuses to condemn an innocent scout merely to preserve an alliance built on protecting a traitor. In a different hypothetical, he accepts letting a friend rest rather than killing another person to bring them back. His principle is not that every loss can be prevented. It is that command must not make someone else’s life a convenient thing to spend.

He trusts Thorn because they have fought together and he believes she is good. He also respects Kasiri’s balance of reason and feeling, while admitting he does not know Pin well enough to promise allegiance. These judgments are his view at the test, not a verdict on everyone’s later conduct.

Learning what pain can teach, and what it cannot

In the arena Modeli attacks Kasiri while she is occupied and hopes she will still consider him an ally afterward. He wants his weaknesses exposed in a setting where failing can teach him something before a real battle.

The lesson is brutal. He keeps advancing while battered and exhausted, repeats that he is not down yet and eventually falls. When he gets up, he is in no condition to turn immediately to the leadership discussion. Willingness to endure has limits in a body that is still bleeding. The test does not prove that training has made him ready for every danger.

Following a chosen company without becoming certain

At the later field test, Modeli still resents being talked down to when the candidates have already faced real loss. He nevertheless follows Severina’s direction. He is uneasy with reinforcing the role of a single leader, but recognizes that the group has chosen a route and he must commit to acting with it.

Near Delerium he wants to flee back to his books. Instead he urges the company to protect companions who may not understand the danger and holds his ground despite fear. His insistence that they must all come home is a commitment made under pressure, not evidence by itself that every expedition ends as he hopes.

Work beyond proving himself

Later Modeli tries, awkwardly, to cheer a companion and reminds people to drink. He approaches Melian with an offer of work, carrying equipment the company found in her old home, and tells her he can show her family’s graves.

The same person who wants to be worthy of divine trust also has to learn ordinary reassurance and careful service to another person’s history. His role in the Veilguard remains tied to those choices, not simply to Mya’s prediction of what power he might one day possess.
